work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu IV.2 note 10 · Mourning Worn at the Changing of the Grave … The Texture of the Cloth of Coat and Hat

items.text: When acting for your father in family affairs, wear the ssi mourning.
items.quote: An uncapped youth does not wear the ssi mourning, unless he is acting for his father in the direction of the family affairs.

items.text: Mourn your own brothers as if you were an ordinary person.
items.quote: The concubine of a man of whatever rank wears mourning for her own brothers and cousins as if she were only an ordinary person.

items.text: Mourn your own cousins as if you were an ordinary person.
items.quote: The concubine of a man of whatever rank wears mourning for her own brothers and cousins as if she were only an ordinary person.

items.text: For your parents, wear a common hairpin with a head and fasten your hair in a loose roll.
items.quote: A married daughter wears for her parents, and a wife for her parentsin-law, a common hairpin with a head to it, and fastens her hair in a loose roll.

items.text: For your parents-in-law, wear a common hairpin with a head and fasten your hair in a loose roll.
items.quote: A married daughter wears for her parents, and a wife for her parentsin-law, a common hairpin with a head to it, and fastens her hair in a loose roll.

items.text: When the wailing is finished, break off the head of the hairpin and put on a cloth coif.
items.quote: When the wailing is finished, the daughter breaks the head off a hairpin, and, pinning up her hair, puts on a cloth coif.

items.text: Wear the common hairpin to the end of the obsequies for your parents-in-law.
items.quote: Because the wife wears the common hairpin to the end of the obsequies.

items.text: For your lord's wife, wear a common hairpin with a head and a cloth coif.
items.quote: A concubine wears for her lord’s wife, and for his eldest son, a common hairpin with a head, and a cloth coif.

items.text: For your lord's eldest son, wear a common hairpin with a head and a cloth coif.
items.quote: A concubine wears for her lord’s wife, and for his eldest son, a common hairpin with a head, and a cloth coif.

work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu IV.1 · The Ssu-ma Mourning for Three Months … The Mourning of a Concubine’s Son for His Adopted Mother's Family

items.text: Wear the ssu-ma mourning for three months for your own mother.
items.quote: A son by a concubine who has become his father’s successor wears it for his own mother.

items.text: Wear ssu-ma mourning for your mother, if she was a concubine.
items.quote: An ordinary officer wears it for his mother, if she was a concubine.

items.text: Wear ssu-ma mourning for your nursing-mother.
items.quote: A man wears it for his nursing-mother.

items.text: Wear ssu-ma mourning for your son-in-law.
items.quote: And for his son-in-law.

items.text: Wear ssu-ma mourning for your parents-in-law.
items.quote: And for his parents-in-law.

items.text: Wear ssu-ma mourning for your maternal uncles.
items.quote: And for his maternal uncles.

items.text: Wear ssu-ma mourning for your uncles' sons.
items.quote: Also for his uncles’ sons.

items.text: Wear ssu-ma mourning for your husband's paternal aunts who died in mature youth.
items.quote: A woman wears it for her husband’s paternal aunts, elder and younger, who have died in mature youth.

items.text: Wear mourning one degree above ordinary for a brother who died while residing abroad with you.
items.quote: If two brothers are residing abroad in the same State, and one should die, the other wears mourning for him a degree above the ordinary.

work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu I.1 · The Three Years’ Untrimmed Mourning

items.text: Wear three years' untrimmed mourning for your father.
items.quote: This mourning is worn for a father.

items.text: For your father's death, live in a mourning booth, sleep on straw, wail day and night, and eat only congee morning and evening.
items.quote: He wails day and night, with no set times. For food he sups up congee, made twice a day, morning and evening, with one handful of grain.

items.text: If still at home, wear three years' untrimmed mourning for your father, using a grass-cloth binder, bamboo hairpin, and letting hair down.
items.quote: If a daughter be still at home, she wears it for her father.

items.text: If after marriage you return to your father's house, wear this mourning for him.
items.quote: If a girl after marriage returns to her father's house, she wears this mourning for her father.

items.text: Wear three years' untrimmed mourning for your husband.
items.quote: A wife wears this mourning for her husband.

items.text: Wear three years' untrimmed mourning for your heir, because he represents the ancestors.
items.quote: A father wears it for his heir.

items.text: Wear three years' untrimmed mourning for the person you have adopted to succeed you.
items.quote: A man wears it for the person whom he has adopted to succeed him.

items.text: Mourn for the grandparents and wife and her relatives of the man who adopted you, acting as a regular son.
items.quote: The adopted heir wears mourning for the grandparents of the man whom he succeeds, and for his wife, his wife's father, mother, and brothers

items.text: As a concubine, wear three years' untrimmed mourning for your lord and master.
items.quote: A concubine wears it for her lord and master.
items.conflict: Concubinage is contrary to Scripture: marriage is one man and one woman.

work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu II.2 · The Year of Trimmed Mourning without the Staff

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your deceased grandfather and grandmother.
items.quote: Is worn for the grandfather and grandmother

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your deceased paternal uncles and their wives.
items.quote: It is worn for elder and younger paternal uncles and their wives
items.needs_role: elder and younger paternal uncles and their wives

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your deceased paternal aunts.
items.quote: Why is this mourning worn for older and younger paternal aunts? They owe it to their husband’s name which they bear.

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your deceased brothers.
items.quote: A man wears it for his brothers.

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for all your sons except the heir.
items.quote: For all his sons except his heir.

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your nephews and unmarried nieces.
items.quote: And for his nephews and unmarried nieces.

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your grandson who is in the line of succession.
items.quote: A man wears it for his grandson in the succession.

items.text: If adopted as successor to another, wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your own father and mother.
items.quote: One who has been adopted as the successor to another wears this mourning for his own father and mother as an act of grace.

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your deceased father and mother, and for the brother who succeeds your father.
items.quote: A married daughter wears it for her father and mother, and for him among her brothers who succeeds her father.
items.needs_role: father and mother, and brother who succeeds father

items.text: If you lived with a stepfather, observe this mourning for him.
items.quote: If he live with his stepfather, a son observes this mourning for him.

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your husband's nephews.
items.quote: A woman wears it for her husband’s nephews.

items.text: Wear trimmed mourning without the staff for your deceased parents-in-law.
items.quote: A woman wears it for her father- and motherin-law.

work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu I.2 · The Trimmed Sackcloth Mourning … The Trimmed Mourning with the Staff

items.text: Wear the three-year trimmed mourning with staff for your mother if your father is already dead.
items.quote: If the father be already dead, it is worn for the mother.

items.text: Mourn for your stepmother as you would for your own mother.
items.quote: A son mourns for his stepmother as he does for his mother.

items.text: Mourn for your foster-mother as you would your own mother.
items.quote: A son mourns his foster-mother as he does his own mother.

items.text: Wear the three-year trimmed mourning for your son who is the heir.
items.quote: A mother wears this mourning for the heir.

items.text: If your father is still alive, wear the one-year trimmed mourning for your mother.
items.quote: While the father is still alive this mourning is assumed on the death of the mother.

items.text: Abstain from taking another wife for three years after your wife's death, out of regard for your son's feelings.
items.quote: The father shall abstain from taking another wife for three years... as an indication that he appreciates the feelings of his son.

items.text: Wear the one-year trimmed mourning for your deceased wife.
items.quote: A husband wears it for his wife.

items.text: If your mother was divorced, wear the one-year trimmed mourning for her.
items.quote: The son of a divorced wife wears it for his mother.

items.text: If your father has appointed you as his successor, do not wear mourning for your divorced mother.
items.quote: If the son of the divorced wife have been appointed by the father as his successor, then he does not wear mourning for his mother.

items.text: Children who follow their remarried stepmother to her new home shall wear the one-year trimmed mourning for her when she dies.
items.quote: If the father have died, and his stepmother have married again, the children who follow her to her new home wear this mourning for her when she dies.

work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu III.2 · The Ta-kung Mourning Worn for Nine Months … The Sui Mourning which is Taken Off After the Burial

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for your own brothers.
items.quote: A man adopted by another as his successor wears it for his own brothers.

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for your grandsons who are not in the succession.
items.quote: A man wears it for his grandsons if they are not in the succession.

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for the wife of your son who is in the succession.
items.quote: And for the wife of his son in the succession,

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for all your brothers.
items.quote: Married daughters wear it for all their brothers.

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for your nephews and nieces as an act of grace.
items.quote: They also wear it for their nephews and nieces as an act of grace.

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for your husband's grandparents.
items.quote: A wife wears it for her husband’s grandparents,

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for your husband's elder and younger uncles and their wives.
items.quote: and elder and younger uncles and their wives.

items.text: If you are a great officer, wear the ta-kung mourning for your elder and younger uncles and aunts, if they hold the rank of ordinary officer.
items.quote: A great officer wears it for his elder and younger uncles and aunts, ... provided that they hold the rank of ordinary officer.

items.text: If you are a great officer, wear the ta-kung mourning for your children other than the eldest, if they hold the rank of ordinary officer.
items.quote: A great officer wears it for ... his children, other than the eldest, ... provided that they hold the rank of ordinary officer.

items.text: If you are a great officer, wear the ta-kung mourning for your brothers, if they hold the rank of ordinary officer.
items.quote: A great officer wears it for ... his brothers ... provided that they hold the rank of ordinary officer.

items.text: If you are a great officer, wear the ta-kung mourning for your brothers' children, if they hold the rank of ordinary officer.
items.quote: A great officer wears it for ... his brothers and their children, provided that they hold the rank of ordinary officer.

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for the married daughters of your husband's brothers.
items.quote: A woman wears it for the married daughters of her husband’s brothers.

work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu II.3 · The Trimmed Mourning Worn for Three Months … The Ta-kung Worn for Early Death, for Nine or Seven Months’ Mourning

items.text: Wear the three months' trimmed mourning for the heir of the main line, his mother, and his wife.
items.quote: The men and women of the family wear it for the son who is in the succession of the great head of the family, and for his mother and wife.
items.needs_role: lineage heir, his mother, his wife

items.text: If you did not live with your stepfather, still wear the three months' trimmed mourning for him.
items.quote: A man wears it for his stepfather if he has not been living with him.

items.text: As a great-grandchild, wear the three months' trimmed mourning for your great-grandparents.
items.quote: And for his great-grandparents.

items.text: If your son who is the heir of the main line dies, wear the three months' trimmed mourning if he was adult, or the ta-kung mourning if he died in youth.
items.quote: The great officer wears it in the case of the death of his son who was successor to the great head of the family.

items.text: Whether married or unmarried, wear the three months' trimmed mourning for your grandparents.
items.quote: A married or an unmarried daughter wears this mourning for her grandparents.

items.text: Mourn a child who dies in mature or middle youth with the ta-kung mourning.
items.quote: It is worn for a child, boy or girl, who has died in mature or middle youth.

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for a younger uncle or a paternal aunt who died in mature or middle youth.
items.quote: a younger uncle, older and younger paternal aunts

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for a brother who died in mature or middle youth.
items.quote: brothers older and younger

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for your husband's nephews and nieces who died in mature or middle youth.
items.quote: a husband’s nephews and nieces
items.needs_role: husband's nephews/nieces who died in youth

items.text: Wear the ta-kung mourning for a grandson in the succession who died in mature or middle youth.
items.quote: It is worn for a grandson in the succession
items.needs_role: grandson in succession who died in youth

items.text: As a son of a concubine, wear the ta-kung mourning for your legitimate brother who died in mature or middle youth.
items.quote: the sons of great officers by concubines wear it for their brothers born of the wife
items.needs_role: legitimate brother who died in youth

items.text: Give your child a name when he is three months old.
items.quote: when a child is three months old, the father gives it a name

work: Mourning Garments, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial
heading: Yili 11 · Sang Fu 喪服 · Mourning Garments (Steele, chapters XXII-XXV) · Sang Fu III.4 · The Hsiao-kung Mourning Worn for Five Months for Those Who Die Early … The Five Months Hsiao-kung Mourning

items.text: Wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for your younger paternal uncles, a grandson in the succession, a brother, and your paternal aunts and unmarried sisters who die in early youth.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: a man wears it for his paternal aunts and unmarried sisters who die in early youth

items.text: Wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for your grand-uncle and his wife, your uncle once removed and his wife, your second cousins, your married female first cousins, and your married granddaughters.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: A man wears it for his grand-uncle and his wife, and his uncle once removed and his wife.

items.text: As a son of a great officer by a concubine, wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for your brothers by the wife who die in early youth.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: The son of a great officer by a concubine wears it in the same circumstances for his brothers by the wife
items.needs_role: son of a great officer by a concubine

items.text: As one adopted as successor to another, wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for your original brothers and first cousins if they die in mature youth, your married sisters, your maternal grandparents, and your maternal aunt once removed and her husband.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: A man who is adopted as the successor of another wears it for his brothers, and first cousins if they die in mature youth.

items.text: Wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for your husband's younger paternal uncles who die in mature youth, your brothers' and husband's brothers' sons and daughters who die in early youth, your nephews and grandsons not in the succession and their wives, your husband's paternal aunts, and the wives of his elder and younger brothers.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: It is worn by a wife for her husband’s younger paternal uncles when they die in mature youth.

items.text: As a great officer, brother of a Duke, or son of a great officer, wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for your brothers, sons by concubines, unmarried paternal aunts and daughters who die in mature youth, and for your first cousins' grandsons not in the succession and your paternal aunts and daughters married to ordinary officers.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: A great officer, the brothers of a Duke, and the sons of a great officer, wear this mourning for... their brothers, their sons by concubines, their unmarried paternal aunts and daughters.
items.needs_role: great officer, brother of a Duke, or son of a great officer

items.text: As a concubine of a great officer, wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for your lord's son not in the succession who dies in mature youth, his married daughters by concubines, the wives of his sons not in the succession, and the father, mother, and sisters of the ruler's mother.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: The concubine of a great officer wears it for his married daughters by concubines.

items.text: As a grandson of a ruler, wear the five-month hsiao-kung mourning for the concubine of your father who wet-nursed you.
items.citation: Yili 11 · Sang Fu, Sang Fu III.4
items.quote: The grandson of a ruler wears it for the concubine of his father, who wet-nursed him.
